name: The Forbidden City (Imperial Palace)
description: The world's largest palatial complex, spanning 720,000 square meters with 980 surviving buildings and 8,886 bays of rooms.
history: Served as the home of 24 Chinese emperors across the Ming and Qing Dynasties from 1420 to 1924 CE.
construction: Built by over one million workers using precision interlocking timber bracket joinery (Dougong) without a single iron nail.
architecture: Strict North-South axial Feng Shui alignment, yellow glazed imperial roof tiles, white marble terraces, and deep crimson walls.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987; the supreme monument of traditional Chinese architecture.
currentStatus: Standing pristine as the Palace Museum in the heart of Beijing.
